Definition: a (male) calf (as frisking round), especially one nearly grown (i.e. a steer)
BiblicalUsage: A calf is a young bull, and in the Bible it is most often an idol, the shape men's hands give to a god they can see. Aaron fashions a golden calf while Moses is on the mountain, Jeroboam sets up two calves at Dan and Bethel and tells Israel these are the gods that brought them out of Egypt, and Hosea says the calf of Samaria will be broken in pieces. The animal is innocent; the worship is the sin.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe idolatry always makes God smaller than He is, because a calf can be carried, melted, and broken, and the true God cannot. I hold that anything I shape to control God is a calf, and I want no part of it.
